title: Choosing Parts
summary: Match the CPU, motherboard, RAM, storage, case, GPU, PSU, and cooler before buying anything.
actions: Choose a CPU platform first, then match the motherboard socket and chipset.
Check RAM generation, case size, GPU length, cooler height, and PSU wattage.
Reserve part of the budget for airflow, storage, and a reliable power supply.
mistakes: Buying DDR4 RAM for a DDR5-only motherboard.
Choosing a case that does not fit the GPU or motherboard form factor.

title: Preparing Tools
summary: Set up a clean, bright workspace with the right tools and a simple anti-static habit.
actions: Prepare a Phillips screwdriver, cable ties, thermal paste if needed, and a tray for screws.
Build on a solid table with good lighting and keep manuals within reach.
Touch the unpainted metal case frame before handling sensitive parts.
mistakes: Building on carpet with parts scattered around.
Losing motherboard standoff screws before the board is mounted.

title: Installing CPU
summary: Seat the processor gently by aligning the triangle marker or socket notches.
actions: Open the socket retention arm or frame.
Align the CPU marker with the socket marker and lower it without sliding.
Lock the retention mechanism and keep the socket cover for warranty support.
mistakes: Touching the contact pads or socket pins.
Forcing the CPU when it is not aligned.

title: Installing RAM
summary: Install memory in the recommended slots so dual-channel mode works correctly.
actions: Open the DIMM latches and check the slot order in the motherboard manual.
Align the notch and press evenly until the latch clicks.
Use slots A2 and B2 first on most two-stick builds.
mistakes: Using adjacent slots when the manual recommends alternating slots.
Stopping before the module is fully seated.

title: Installing SSD
summary: Install the M.2 drive under its heatsink, then secure it without overtightening.
actions: Remove the M.2 heatsink or screw from the correct slot.
Insert the SSD at an angle and press it down onto the standoff.
Reinstall the heatsink after removing any protective film from the thermal pad.
mistakes: Leaving plastic film on a heatsink thermal pad.
Using the wrong standoff position for the SSD length.

title: Mounting Motherboard
summary: Install standoffs, align the rear I/O, and secure the board evenly.
actions: Confirm the case standoffs match the motherboard size.
Lower the board into the case without scraping the rear I/O area.
Tighten screws in a gentle cross pattern.
mistakes: Leaving an extra standoff under the board.
Overtightening screws and flexing the PCB.

title: Installing GPU
summary: Seat the graphics card in the primary PCIe slot and secure it to the case.
actions: Remove the correct rear expansion slot covers.
Unlock the PCIe latch, align the card, and press until fully seated.
Support heavier cards and fasten the bracket screws.
mistakes: Forgetting to remove slot covers before pushing the GPU in.
Plugging the monitor into the motherboard instead of the GPU.

title: Connecting PSU Cables
summary: Route only the needed modular cables and make every power connector click.
actions: Connect 24-pin motherboard power, 8-pin CPU power, GPU power, SATA power if needed, and front-panel leads.
Route cables through the nearest grommets to keep airflow clear.
Check that PCIe and CPU EPS cables are not swapped.
mistakes: Missing the CPU power connector near the top of the motherboard.
Using one daisy-chained GPU cable for a high-power graphics card.

title: First Boot
summary: Start with minimal peripherals and watch for fan spin, display output, and debug LEDs.
actions: Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse, and power cable.
Turn on the PSU switch and press the case power button.
If there is no display, check RAM seating, GPU power, and debug LEDs.
mistakes: Panicking during the first long memory-training boot.
Troubleshooting without reading the motherboard debug indicator.

title: BIOS Setup
summary: Verify hardware detection, enable memory profile, set boot order, and update firmware when needed.
actions: Confirm CPU, RAM, SSD, and fan readings appear correctly.
Enable EXPO or XMP for rated memory speed.
Set USB install media as the first boot device.
mistakes: Leaving fast RAM at default JEDEC speed.
Updating BIOS during unstable power conditions.

title: Installing Windows/Linux
summary: Install the operating system, chipset drivers, GPU drivers, and core updates.
actions: Create a bootable USB installer for Windows or your Linux distribution.
Install to the primary SSD and remove the USB when setup restarts.
Install chipset, network, audio, and GPU drivers after the desktop loads.
mistakes: Installing the OS on the wrong drive.
Skipping chipset drivers and blaming the hardware for unstable behavior.
